summary: Train to govern social protection registration, eligibility, payments and grievance redress. Build practical safeguards and reform plans. Explore the course.
lede: Digital social protection delivery depends on coordinated oversight of registration, eligibility, payments, case management and grievance resolution. For programme directors, registry managers and public-sector operations teams, this course develops practical approaches to improving delivery across programmes and institutions. Participants map responsibilities, assess inclusion and eligibility controls, monitor payment and grievance indicators, and create data-sharing safeguards and a sequenced reform roadmap through exercises such as delivery-chain mapping and an Excel-based dashboard.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who set policy, manage programme operations or oversee the public systems that deliver social protection. It is especially relevant when you coordinate multiple agencies, delivery partners or funding requirements. This course is designed for: Social protection programme directors overseeing end-to-end delivery performance. Social assistance operations managers coordinating enrolment, payments and case resolution. Social registry managers governing registration quality and update processes. Grievance-redress managers monitoring complaints, appeals and resolution timelines. Eligibility policy specialists documenting assessment rules and decision controls. Digital transformation leads coordinating interoperability across public agency systems. Payment operations officers reconciling transfers and investigating exception records. Social protection data-governance officers reviewing access, sharing and retention arrangements. Donor-funded programme managers aligning delivery reforms with programme results frameworks. Public service inclusion advisers assessing access barriers across delivery channels.
modules: World Bank Social Protection Delivery Systems
NIST Privacy Framework and Data Exchange
prerequisites: Working familiarity with social protection programmes, public-service operations or programme delivery is recommended. No coding or software engineering experience is required. Exercises use governance scenarios and basic spreadsheet functions; advanced analytics and system configuration are outside the course scope.
